keywords.def: document listing someone's education, qualifications and work experience, which is written when looking for a job

keywords.term: the worst they can do is say no
keywords.def: phrase meaning 'don't be afraid of trying to do something for fear of rejection'
something typical or associated with a particular person or place; something a person or place is known for
be very noticeable or better compared to other similar things

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. Do you enjoy cooking Neil?
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Becca。Neil，你喜欢做饭吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I do enjoy cooking. I think it's quite relaxing, especially after a busy day.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实喜欢做饭。我觉得这挺让人放松的，尤其是在忙碌了一天之后。

sentences.en: How about you, Becca? I enjoy cooking when I'm feeding other people, but usually after a busy day at work, I don't enjoy cooking for myself.
sentences.zh: 你呢，Becca？如果是做给别人吃，我挺喜欢做饭的，但通常在忙碌的工作日结束后，我不太喜欢给自己做饭。

sentences.en: Well, we're talking about cooking today, and most of us can at least boil an egg, but not everyone could make it as a professional chef in a world-famous restaurant.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们今天聊聊做饭，虽然我们大多数人至少都会煮个蛋，但并不是每个人都能在世界知名的餐厅里成为一名职业厨师。

sentences.en: Mmm. Being a top chef requires passion, dedication, and hard work.
sentences.zh: 嗯。成为一名顶级厨师需要热情、奉献和艰苦的努力。

sentences.en: Many chefs work 15 hours a day, six days a week, and busy kitchens cooking expensive food are very stressful places to work.
sentences.zh: 许多厨师每天工作15个小时，每周工作六天，而在忙碌、烹饪昂贵食物的厨房里工作，压力是非常大的。

sentences.en: So, why do they do it? In this episode, we'll hear from one South African chef who started her own award-winning restaurant in the country known as the home of fine dining – France.
sentences.zh: 那么，他们为什么要这么做呢？在本期节目中，我们将听到一位南非厨师的故事，她在被称为高级餐饮之乡的国家——法国，开办了自己屡获殊荣的餐厅。

sentences.en: As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我们将学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all this episode's vocabulary, along with a transcript, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的所有词汇以及文本。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 不过首先，我有一个问题要问你，Neil。

sentences.en: The top prizes for any professional chef are Michelin stars, awards given to restaurants offering outstanding cooking.
sentences.zh: 对任何职业厨师来说，最高荣誉就是米其林星级，这是颁发给提供杰出烹饪的餐厅的奖项。

sentences.en: But who is the winner of the most Michelin stars ever?
sentences.zh: 但是，有史以来获得米其林星级最多的人是谁？

sentences.en: Is it: a) Italian chef Enrico Bartolini, b) French chef Joël Robuchon, or c) British chef Gordon Ramsay?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 意大利厨师 Enrico Bartolini，b) 法国厨师 Joël Robuchon，还是 c) 英国厨师 Gordon Ramsay？

sentences.en: I'm going to say a) the Italian chef Enrico Bartolini, because I went to Italy recently and the food was amazing!
sentences.zh: 我选 a) 意大利厨师 Enrico Bartolini，因为我最近去了趟意大利，那里的食物太棒了！

sentences.en: Mmm! OK. We'll find out the answer later in this episode.
sentences.zh: 嗯！好的。我们稍后将在本期节目中找出答案。

sentences.en: Born in South Africa, chef Chantel Dartnall started her culinary career at a three-Michelin-star restaurant in the exclusive Mayfair area of London.
sentences.zh: 厨师 Chantel Dartnall 出生于南非，她的烹饪生涯始于伦敦高档的 Mayfair 地区的一家米其林三星级餐厅。

sentences.en: Here, she tells Ruth Alexander, presenter of BBC World Service programme The Food Chain, how it all got started: What happened is I had graduated from the Prue Leith College of Food and Wine and decided to send my CV to all the three-Michelin-star restaurants that I could find at that moment in the Michelin Guide.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 的主持人 Ruth Alexander 讲述了这一切是如何开始的：“当时的情况是，我刚从 Prue Leith College of Food and Wine 毕业，决定把我的 CV 寄给当时我在《米其林指南》中能找到的所有米其林三星级餐厅。”

sentences.en: So, you aimed high from the off. I aimed high.
sentences.zh: “所以，你从一开始就目标高远。”“我确实目标高远。”

sentences.en: The only thing that they could say was no, and what would I lose?
sentences.zh: “他们唯一能做的就是拒绝，而我又会损失什么呢？”

sentences.en: I received a call from chef Paul Rhodes to say, "When can you start?"
sentences.zh: “我接到了厨师 Paul Rhodes 的电话，他说：'你什么时候能开始上班？'”

sentences.en: Wow. And this, sort of, just catapulted my career.
sentences.zh: “哇。这在某种程度上，直接让我的职业生涯飞速发展。”

sentences.en: Chantel sent her CV to the world's top restaurants.
sentences.zh: Chantel 把她的 CV 寄给了世界顶级的餐厅。

sentences.en: CV is short for curriculum vitae, a document listing someone's education, qualifications and work experience, which they write when looking for a job.
sentences.zh: CV 是 curriculum vitae 的缩写，即个人简历，是一份列出某人教育背景、资历和工作经验的文件，在找工作时撰写。

sentences.en: In American English, it's called a résumé.
sentences.zh: 在美式英语中，它被称为 résumé。

sentences.en: Chantel applied to only Michelin-star-winning restaurants.
sentences.zh: Chantel 只申请了获得米其林星级的餐厅。

sentences.en: She aimed high, meaning she was ambitious.
sentences.zh: 她 aimed high，意思是她很有抱复。

sentences.en: Chantel says, " The worst they could do is say no," a phrase which means you shouldn't be afraid of trying to do something because the worst outcome is being rejected.
sentences.zh: Chantel 说：'The worst they could do is say no（他们最坏也就是拒绝）'，这个短语的意思是你不应该害怕尝试去做某事，因为最坏的结果也不过是被拒绝。

sentences.en: Luckily for Chantel, the answer was yes, and learning her trade in a top London restaurant catapulted, meaning accelerated, her career.
sentences.zh: 对 Chantel 来说幸运的是，答案是肯定的，在伦敦一家顶级餐厅学习手艺 catapulted（意思是加速了）她的职业生涯。

sentences.en: At the age of 26, Chantel left London and returned home to open her own restaurant, Mosaic, near Pretoria in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 26岁时，Chantel 离开伦敦回到家乡，在南非 Pretoria 附近开办了自己的餐厅 Mosaic。

sentences.en: She'd been inspired by botanical cuisine, the use of edible flowers and herbs to decorate and flavour food.
sentences.zh: 她受到了植物料理（botanical cuisine）的启发，即使用食用花卉和草药来装饰食物并为其调味。

sentences.en: Here, Chantel tells more to BBC World Service programme The Food Chain: When I opened Mosaic in South Africa, I knew I wanted something entirely different and something which diners had not seen.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Chantel 向 BBC World Service 节目 The Food Chain 透露了更多细节：“当我在南非开办 Mosaic 时，我知道我想要一些完全不同的、食客们从未见过的东西。”

sentences.en: I wanted to have my own signature and to stand out, and I think especially for botanical cuisine in South Africa, it was very much unknown.
sentences.zh: “我想要有自己的 signature（招牌/特色）并脱颖而出，而且我认为，尤其是在南非，植物料理在当时还非常不为人知。”

sentences.en: Chantel developed her own signature. A signature item is something that is typical of, or strongly associated with, a particular person or place.
sentences.zh: Chantel 发展出了她自己的 signature。Signature item（招牌产品）是指代表某个人或地方，或与其有强烈关联的事物。

sentences.en: For example, whisky is Scotland's signature drink.
sentences.zh: 例如，威士忌是苏格兰的招牌饮料。

sentences.en: Chantel's signature is cooking botanical food.
sentences.zh: Chantel 的招牌是烹饪植物料理。

sentences.en: Chantel's Mosaic restaurant is currently at the Château des Tesnières in northern France, where it's listed among the top 200 restaurants in the world.
sentences.zh: Chantel 的 Mosaic 餐厅目前位于法国北部的 Château des Tesnières，在那里它被列为世界前200家餐厅之一。

sentences.en: And in 2017 she won the title Best Female Chef in the World.
sentences.zh: 在2017年，她赢得了“世界最佳女厨师”的称号。

sentences.en: These achievements have helped Chantel stand out – to be more noticeable and better than other chefs.
sentences.zh: 这些成就帮助 Chantel stand out——也就是比其他厨师更引人注目、更优秀。

sentences.en: Chantel is still waiting, but surely it's only a matter of time until she wins those coveted Michelin stars.
sentences.zh: Chantel 仍在等待，但她获得那些梦寐以求的米其林星级肯定只是时间问题。

sentences.en: Speaking of which, what was the answer to your question, Becca?
sentences.zh: 说到这个，Becca，你那个问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: Ah yes, I asked you earlier, "Who is the winner of the most Michelin stars ever?"
sentences.zh: 啊是的，我之前问过你：'有史以来获得米其林星级最多的人是谁？'

sentences.en: I said that it was the Italian chef Enrico Bartolini...
sentences.zh: 我说是意大利厨师 Enrico Bartolini……

sentences.en: ...but unfortunately, it was incorrect. Oh no!
sentences.zh: ……但很遗憾，答错了。哦，不！

sentences.en: The right answer is b) Joël Robuchon, our French chef with 31 stars – the most decorated chef in history.
sentences.zh: 正确答案是 b) Joël Robuchon，这位法国厨师拥有31颗星——是历史上获得荣誉最多的厨师。

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with curriculum vitae, CV, or résumé in American English – a document outlining someone's education, qualifications and work experience, which they prepare when looking for a job.
sentences.zh: 好了。让我们复习一下学过的词汇，首先是 curriculum vitae，简称 CV，在美式英语中是 résumé——即个人简历，是一份概述某人教育背景、资历和工作经验的文件，在找工作时准备。

sentences.en: To aim high means to be ambitious and set high goals.
sentences.zh: To aim high 意思是很有抱负并设定高目标。

sentences.en: The phrase the worst they can do is say no means 'don't be afraid of trying to do something for the fear of rejection'.
sentences.zh: 短语 the worst they can do is say no 意思是“不要因为害怕被拒绝而不敢尝试去做某事”。

sentences.en: If something is catapulted, it's suddenly accelerated or launched forward.
sentences.zh: 如果某事被 catapulted，意思就是它突然被加速或向前推进。

sentences.en: A signature item is something that a person or place is known for.
sentences.zh: A signature item 是指某人或某地因其而闻名的事物。

sentences.en: And finally, to stand out means to be more noticeable or better than other similar things.
sentences.zh: 最后，to stand out 意思是比其他类似的事物更引人注目或更好。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed this episode, you'll find a quiz and worksheet to practise the vocabulary we've learnt on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。如果你喜欢本期节目，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到测试和工作单，来练习我们学过的词汇。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 我们很快会再见。不过现在，要说再见了。

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
